title: How to pick where to advertise: measurable, quick, cheap, comfortable
summary: After running a hundred ad campaigns at Smart Bear across paid search, trade shows, mailers, newsletters and print, Jason Cohen concluded he could not predict which would work. His fix is to rank options by measurability, speed of learning, low cost and personal comfort, then start and test rather than agonize over the "right" channel.

principles.text: You can't predict which ad channel will work; only accurate measurement plus a real trial tells you.
principles.quote: I learned I have zero ability at predicting which campaigns would produce. The only way to tell was to ensure accurate measurement was in place and try it.

principles.text: Negotiate a lower first-time rate for the trial of any new ad channel.
principles.quote: And negotiate a lower "first time" rate for the trial.

principles.text: Channel quality decays over time, so keep re-measuring and push prices down as results fall, whatever the seller's audience stats say.
principles.quote: But as the years wore on it became less and less effective, like clockwork, and I kept demanding a lower and lower price.

principles.text: First priority when choosing a channel: measurable. You must know objectively whether the value gained exceeds the money spent.
principles.quote: you have to know objectively if the value to your company is greater than the amount of money spent.

principles.text: Early on, optimize for fast, cheap learning about what advertising works, not total revenue; scale spend once you know how money turns into more money.
principles.quote: At this stage the valuable thing is seeking/learning what advertising works, not trying to maximize total revenue right out of the gate.

principles.text: Since your gut can't predict winners, pick channels you know and like, where you understand the culture and can craft a fitting ad.
principles.quote: Since your gut isn't too useful, you might as well pick something you like, especially if you already understand the culture of the site
